what: a cost test prints its counter table with println!, but the runner shows a test's output only when it fails, so reading the counters after a change took a temporary panic! at the end of the test, one extra queue round, and care to remove it before the admitting ask. Separately, blaze-solve has two traits named Source (facts::Source, the pull, and assembly::Source, a candidate's origin), so eval.rs imports the first as FactSource.
cost: three extra queue rounds (about 3 minutes each) and the risk of admitting a test that always panics
cause: the runner reports pass/fail lines only; a measurement test has no channel for its numbers on a pass
whys: the queue was built for verdicts, not for measurements; cost tests are both
class: a measurement read through a failure: any counter wanted on a pass has to fail a test to be seen
prevention: wanted: `runner.py ask --show <test>` printing a named test's stdout on a pass, or the runner keeping each test's stdout in a file named in its answer
annoyance: temporary panics to see counters; two traits named Source in one crate
workaround: a panic!("...TEMPORARY...") removed before the admitting ask
